title: The Terminal of Kepler Reach Revisited
premise: Tamsin Nystrom, a terraformer and courier on the long route between the silent colonies of Kepler Reach, tends a garden seeded for future generations while keeping their own past carefully buried. When a distress signal arrives in a language extinct for two centuries, Tamsin traces it to a hidden cryoship carrying two rival halves of humanity's last diaspora—each faction's survival protocols requiring the other's extinction. As the Reach's powers converge on the ship, Tamsin must choose which half wakes, discovering that the signal was sent by their own grandmother, who engineered the crisis to force a third option: waking neither, and instead birthing a new generation from the garden itself. In the end, Tamsin sacrifices the courier route that defined them, broadcasting the truth of both factions' crimes so that whoever wakes—decades hence—will inherit honesty rather than victory.
about_author: Beatrix Oyelaran is a former botanist who spent five years cataloguing seed banks in remote research stations before turning to fiction full-time. Her work explores inheritance, ecological grief, and the stories we leave for people we will never meet.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Tamsin Nystrom pilots the courier vessel Vetch between silent colony worlds, tending an onboard seed garden meant for generations not yet born. POV: Tamsin. The beat is quiet competence masking loneliness; we learn they've stopped answering messages from anyone in their past.

chapters.title: Signal in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: A distress transmission arrives in Pre-Exodus Standard, extinct for two centuries, addressed by name to someone called 'the Gardener.' Tamsin, whose grandmother taught them fragments of the language, recognizes the cadence. POV: Tamsin. Emotional beat: dread mixed with an ache of recognition.

chapters.title: What the Garden Remembers
chapters.summary: Tamsin cross-references the signal against inherited family archives, finding their grandmother Ilsa listed as crew on a ship that officially never existed: the Halcyon Vault. POV: Tamsin with flashback interludes. Beat: the first crack in the identity Tamsin built around silence.

chapters.title: Kepler Reach Traffic Control
chapters.summary: Tamsin requests route data from the Reach's bureaucratic hub and attracts the attention of Inspector Dae-Sun Okonkwo, who notices anomalies in the Vetch's flight logs. POV alternates: Tamsin and Dae-Sun. Beat: paranoia—the invisible life begins fraying at the edges.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Debt
chapters.summary: Tamsin visits smuggler-cartographer Ruqayya Vance, who owes them a favor, to triangulate the signal's origin beyond charted space. Ruqayya warns that others are asking the same question. POV: Tamsin. Beat: uneasy alliance; loyalty tested before it's even formed.

chapters.title: Two Hundred Years of Silence
chapters.summary: En route, Tamsin decodes more of the transmission: it describes a schism aboard the generation fleet—one faction chose cryosleep, another chose genetic adaptation—and a protocol requiring one line to erase the other. POV: Tamsin. Beat: horror at realizing the signal is a confession and a countdown.

chapters.title: The Inspector's Ledger
chapters.summary: Dae-Sun Okonkwo, pressured by Reach authorities, opens a formal inquiry into the Vetch, revealing that Tamsin's courier license was issued under a falsified lineage. POV: Dae-Sun. Beat: reluctant duty; she suspects the truth is bigger than her superiors want.

chapters.title: Halcyon Vault
chapters.summary: Tamsin reaches the coordinates and finds the cryoship drifting, hull scarred, garden bays still faintly alive after two centuries. The airlock opens to their grandmother's recorded voice. POV: Tamsin. Beat: awe curdling into grief—Ilsa has been dead a hundred years, but her plan is just beginning.

chapters.title: The Two Cradles
chapters.summary: Inside, Tamsin discovers two sealed cryo-banks: the Adapted, genetically modified to survive open worlds, and the Pure, unmodified heirs of the old Earth genome. Each bank's wake protocol requires the other's power core. POV: Tamsin. Beat: the impossible arithmetic of survival.

chapters.title: Riders on the Signal
chapters.summary: Ruqayya arrives pursued by Reach enforcers; the signal's broadcast was traced, and three factions now race toward the Vault. POV: Ruqayya. Beat: betrayal or loyalty? She chooses Tamsin, burning her own safe harbor to do it.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Testament
chapters.summary: Tamsin plays Ilsa's final logs: she sabotaged the mutual-annihilation protocol and hid the ship, hoping a descendant would find a third path—but she admits she may have only delayed the killing. POV: Tamsin. Beat: inheritance as burden; anger at being conscripted into an ancestor's war.

chapters.title: Dae-Sun's Choice
chapters.summary: Dae-Sun intercepts the Vetch's beacon and boards the Vault alone, expecting contraband, finding instead the sleeping thousands and Tamsin's evidence of the Reach's founding crime. POV: Dae-Sun. Beat: her loyalty to the institution fractures against the truth.

chapters.title: The Enforcers Arrive
chapters.summary: Reach enforcers breach the Vault, claiming salvage rights over the cryopods; skirmishes break out in the garden bays where Tamsin has been growing food for the waking. POV: ensemble, anchored on Tamsin. Beat: the price of visibility comes due in blood.

chapters.title: Seeds Under Fire
chapters.summary: Tamsin defends the seed archive rather than the cryopods, a choice that horrifies Ruqayya until Tamsin explains: the pods can be moved, but the garden is the only thing that makes waking survivable. POV: Tamsin. Beat: conviction hardening into sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Arithmetic of Waking
chapters.summary: Power calculations show only one cryo-bank can be revived before the Vault's reactor fails. Both factions' surviving representatives—reached by relay—demand their people be chosen. POV: alternating transmissions. Beat: the moral cliff edge; every option is a massacre.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Meant
chapters.summary: Tamsin decodes the final layer of Ilsa's message: the 'third option' isn't choosing—it's germination. The Vault's gene-banks and the garden together could grow children outside both factions' definitions of purity. POV: Tamsin. Beat: revelation as relief and terror; it requires decades no one present will live to see.

chapters.title: The Bargain at Airlock Nine
chapters.summary: Tamsin brokers a fragile truce: the enforcers get the Vault's reactor data, Dae-Sun gets the truth on record, and the factions agree to a supervised partial waking of both banks—in exchange for Tamsin surrendering the Vetch and the route. POV: ensemble. Beat: diplomacy at gunpoint; trust extended against all instinct.

chapters.title: Reactor Fall
chapters.summary: During the transfer, the failing reactor cascades; Tamsin stays behind to hand-stabilize the garden bay's climate systems while the first waking pods are evacuated. POV: Tamsin. Beat: climax—survival finally costs something real, and Tamsin pays it willingly.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: From the dying Vault, Tamsin transmits the complete history of the schism, the Reach's complicity, and Ilsa's testament to every world on the long route. POV: Tamsin. Beat: truth as inheritance; the silence ends forever.

chapters.title: Aftermath: The Reach Answers
chapters.summary: The broadcast detonates across the colonies; Dae-Sun survives politically by becoming its chief witness, while factions scramble to claim or condemn the Vault's children. POV: Dae-Sun. Beat: consequences rippling outward; justice begins as exposure, not verdicts.

chapters.title: The First Green
chapters.summary: Months later, the first vault-born children open their eyes in a habitat built around Tamsin's rescued garden—neither Adapted nor Pure, simply new. Tamsin, injured and grounded, teaches them the old language. POV: Tamsin. Beat: quiet wonder; the garden finally has its people.

chapters.title: Route's End, Route's Beginning
chapters.summary: Tamsin plants Ilsa's final seed packet and writes a letter to the future, accepting that some harvests belong to hands they'll never shake. The long route continues without them, but the Reach speaks again. POV: Tamsin, closing epilogue voice. Beat: peace earned through loss; inheritance fulfilled.
